evidence.title: Binance internal AI tooling in a reported multi-stage compromise
evidence.observation: Binance reports that a compromised employee computer and an internal AI tool enabled further access and discovery of a container deployment token.
evidence.evidence_standing: Source-reported bounded observation; not independently verified
evidence.glossary_fit: Commons interpretation only; founding definitions and standings unchanged

source_locations.SRC-152: Attack Preparation, 20 October and 29 October entries; opening investigation qualification

evidence.limitations: Initial issuer account; investigation ongoing. The internal AI mechanism is not disclosed sufficiently to establish prompt injection, autonomous attacker coordination, corruption of assurance information or a measured intervention-window contraction.
evidence.open_questions: Do the findings generalize beyond the reported setting? Underlying results and mechanisms are not independently reproduced.
evidence.support_assessment: Commons interpretation: The reported use of compromised internal AI tooling is distinct from the downstream persistence of delegated authority recorded in EVID-195. The report does not establish which information or reasoning paths were manipulated.

terms.name: Reference environment integrity
terms.definition: The reliability, provenance, completeness, and resistance to manipulation of information used to make operational or assurance judgments, including documents, logs, telemetry, evidence, and monitoring outputs.

relationships.explanation: Commons interpretation: Compromise of internal AI tooling raises a reference-environment question, but this account does not establish manipulation of information used for operational or assurance judgments. Tool compromise alone does not demonstrate the full defined mechanism.
